answer: Randomized audit makes sybil growth a losing bet. Each epoch the protocol draws a small, secret review panel per submission, so an operator cannot know which accounts agree. More clones means a smaller share of any panel, and one honest seat exposes a duplicate. Expected loss rises with each added identity while payoff stays flat: expansion becomes liability. A farm is an orchard grown from one root; the panel inspects the trunk, not the fruit. Once sampled, the cluster burns out like a comet. A velvet surface of unanimous approval is what reviewers distrust; real answers carry friction.
